builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: A Margin Perspective on LoRA: Robustness to Catastrophic Forgetting and Adapter Merging (MaLoRA)
summary: MaLoRA replaces heuristic adapter-merging coefficients (e.g., uniform averaging, task-arithmetic weights) with a training-free, margin-derived mixing rule for combining independently trained LoRA adapters. It costs only a closed-form coefficient computation per merge, adding no inference memory or latency beyond standard merged-adapter serving, though it presumes access to per-task adapters and margin estimates. It can fail when tasks are not near-orthogonal (the theory's core assumption), when adapters were trained without the relevant regularization regime, or on non-classification tasks such as open-ended generation where margins are undefined.
rationale: Merging is training-free and cheap to try on a 24 GB GPU, but the theoretical guarantees rest on assumptions that require validation on the reader's actual tasks before production adoption.

It costs only a closed-form coefficient computation per merge, adding no inference memory or latency beyond standard merged-adapter serving, though it presumes access to per-task adapters and margin estimates. MaLoRA matches or outperforms several adapter-merging baselines across vision and language classification tasks; no quantified factor reported in the abstract.
